blocks.body:
# TacMap — complete feature guide

**TacMap** is the tactical operations map in MiliNav (`TacticalMapV2`). It is the main map screen for tracks, drawings, navigation, terrain measure, overlays, JUPEM offline maps, and sharing.

Open TacMap from the MiliNav home screen. Almost every capability lives under the on-map **Tools** button. The Tools list is searchable — type words such as *compass*, *path*, *overlay*, or *settings*.

## Quick visual

![TacMap feature map](/media/diagrams/tacmap-tools.svg)

This guide explains **every soldier-facing TacMap feature**. Deep math and packaging details stay in the linked pages under this TacMap section.

> **Overlays** vs **JUPEM:** Overlays are *your* layers (tiles, GeoPDF, imported graphics, grid lines). JUPEM files are *official* encrypted TOPO/OSM packages you download or decrypt, then activate as the basemap. They are separate menus on purpose.

---

## How to open tools

1. Open **TacMap**.
2. Tap **Tools** (top / rail). Subtitle: *Tracks, plots, navigation, overlays, share, and settings.*
3. Use the search box to filter by name, description, or keywords.
4. Items with a chevron open a **submenu**. Back returns to Tools.
5. The same overlay list also opens from the **layers** shortcut and the **navigation drawer**.

There is also a **Navigation features** drawer with the navigate / map-look / JUPEM / ops shortcuts. Tools remains the full palette.

---

## Tracks — record where you moved

### Create Track

Starts a movement record you can keep in the **Map Library**.

| Mode | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Start GPS track log** | Follows your phone GPS and draws the path as you move |
| **Draw route** | You sketch the track polyline on the map by hand |
| **Map library** | Opens saved tracks / drawings / photos / offline maps |
| **Stop GPS track** | Ends an active GPS log |

**Typical use:** start a GPS log before a patrol, stop when finished, open Map Library later to review or share.

### Breadcrumbs

Toggle **ON/OFF**. When on, TacMap drops a point on the map each time you move — a dotted trail of where you have been, without managing a full track session.

---

## Plots — drawings and symbols

### Draw Graphics

SketchEditor drawing on the map:

- **Point**, **line**, **area** (polygon), **freehand**, **rectangle**
- Undo / cancel while drawing
- Finished graphics autosave into your local graphics set

Use this for quick field sketches, boundaries, and routes that are not NATO control measures.

### Control Measures

Places **MIL-STD-2525C Appendix B** tactical graphics (control measures) as coded chips — not full unit TO&E icons.

- Colour tells the job (friendly / hostile / neutral / unknown conventions in the picker)
- Search by **name**, **short code**, or **SIDC**
- Place with crosshair or by tapping the map

Full colour and code meanings: [Control Measures](#/control-measures).

---

## Reports — SPOTREP, photos, troops

### SPOTREP

Place a **spot report** on the map:

1. Tap the ground where the observation applies.
2. Add remarks / narrative.
3. Attach **photos**.
4. Keep a **progress log** as the situation updates.

The report stays as a map object you can revisit from your saved content.

### Photo Mode

Pins a **GPS-stamped photo** at your **current location** (needs location permission). Faster than a full SPOTREP when you only need a geotagged picture.

### Troop Tracking

**Coming soon** in the Tools list. Intended for live friendly positions. Do not rely on it for blue-force tracking yet.

---

## Navigate — compass, resection, roads, grid

![Compass bearing navigation](/media/diagrams/compass-bearing.svg)

### Compass Mode (Navigate-To / FastLock)

Walk toward a point with the **FastLock** floating compass.

Typical choices inside the submenu:

- Navigate to a **saved waypoint**
- Navigate to the **map crosshair**
- Enter / leave **compass follow** mode
- **Stop NAV** when finished

Behaviour: the **destination stays fixed**. As you move, bearing and distance are recomputed from **live GPS → same destination**. The needle does not lock the first azimuth forever.

![Live GPS vs fixed course](/media/diagrams/course-modes.svg)

### Compass Bearing (Resection)

Use when GPS is weak or you need a map fix from landmarks:

1. Tap **2 or 3 known landmarks** on the map.
2. TacMap measures forward bearings, draws **back bearings**, and runs **resection**.
3. Tap a **destination**.
4. Follow the floating compass to that destination.

![Two-point resection](/media/diagrams/resection-2pt.svg)

![Three-point resection](/media/diagrams/resection-3pt.svg)

Full formulas and course behaviour: [Compass Bearing Navigation](#/compass-bearing-navigation).

### Get Directions

Road route **A → B**.

| Situation | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Online, OSRM works | Free public road router; drawn on map |
| Online, OSRM fails | May fall back to **ArcGIS World Route** (possible credits) |
| Offline / both fail | Straight-line guidance only |

Start and destination can come from GPS, map drop, crosshair, coordinates, or a waypoint.

Billing detail: [Navigation & ArcGIS Billing](#/navigation-and-arcgis-billing).

![Router billing paths](/media/diagrams/nav-router-billing.svg)

### Go To Grid

Jumps the map camera to a place you type:

- Latitude / longitude
- **UTM**, **MGRS**, and JUPEM-style grid search strings

Does **not** start navigation by itself — it only opens that ground on the map. Combine with Compass Mode or Get Directions if you need to walk there.

### Range & Bearing (also under Measure)

Tap **point A**, then **point B** for geodesic **distance** and **bearing**. Optional rings: **100 m**, **500 m**, **1 km**. Available from Measure & Terrain and from the navigation drawer.

---

## Measure & Terrain

Open **Tools → Measure & Terrain**.

### Distance & Direction

Same range/bearing tool as above (tap A, tap B; optional range rings).

### Can I see it? (Line of sight)

Terrain **line-of-sight** from observer → target:

1. Prefer an **offline GeoTIFF DEM** (Elevation file).
2. If no DEM and the network + ArcGIS key are available, uses **ArcGIS World Elevation** online.
3. Tap **observer**, then **target**.
4. Read whether terrain blocks the line, first obstruction distance, and sample count.

> Terrain awareness only — **not** a fire-control or targeting system.

### Path clearance (Path over the ground)

3D clearance check between two taps:

![Path clearance concept](/media/diagrams/path-clearance.svg)

1. Set elevation source (offline DEM preferred).
2. Optionally set required clearance height (default **50 m**, range 0–5000).
3. Tap **start**, then **end**.
4. TacMap samples ground along the path, builds a clearance arc above the highest ground, and can **replay** a projectile animation.

![Path clearance formula](/media/diagrams/path-clearance-formula.svg)

Full sampling and animation notes: [Path Clearance](#/path-clearance).

> Terrain-only visualisation — **not** fire control.

### Elevation file

Choose or remove the **offline GeoTIFF DEM** used by LOS and path clearance. Without a local DEM, those tools need online elevation (when available).

---

## Map look — basemap and overlays

### Basemap Style

The picture **under** your layers (online styles):

- Satellite
- Streets
- Topographic
- OSM

Changing basemap style does not remove your overlays or JUPEM package state.

### Overlays (your layers)

One list for personal / imported layers. Opens from Tools, the layers shortcut, or the nav drawer.

#### On the map

| Feature | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **Offline Overlays** | Show/hide downloaded tiles, GeoPDF, MBTiles |
| **Grid Lines** | Draw **UTM** or **MGRS** lines on the map |
| **Imported Graphics** | Show, hide, rename, or delete shared battle-graphics layers |
| **Map Library** | Browse drawings, tracks, photos, and offline maps you kept |

#### Import

| Feature | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **Import Battle Graphics** | Open a passphrase-locked `.shua` package as its own non-editable layer |

#### Your map packages

| Feature | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **Download Map Area** | Save the current view for offline use (UI present; treat large areas carefully) |
| **Import GeoPDF Or GeoTIFF** | Add a map sheet you supply over the basemap |
| **Import MBTiles Or TPK** | Add an offline tile pack you supply |

![Map package / offline flow](/media/diagrams/map-package-flow.svg)

---

## JUPEM files — official encrypted maps

Separate from Overlays. These are encrypted TOPO/OSM packages (often on SD card), decrypted on device, then employed as the working basemap.

### Download Or Decrypt

- Download **TOPO** / **OSM** packages (PIN-gated where configured)
- Decrypt a **ZIP on the SD card** (MRSO / BRSO / OSM style packages)
- Reset decrypted cache when you need a clean decrypt

### Activate Map

Employ a decrypted TOPO or OSM **MMPK** as the basemap, or stand it down when you want the online/style basemap again.

### Legacy Nav Map

Opens the classic **Navigation** map (`MainNavigator`) for older workflows. Prefer TacMap for new work.

Storage and decrypt paths: [Storage Paths & Decryption](#/storage-paths-and-decryption).

Desktop packaging of rasters into MMPK: [TIFF to MMPK](#/tiff-to-mmpk).

---

## Share

### Share Battle Graphics

Passphrase-locked **`.shua`** packages for drawings, points, tracks, photos, and reports.

| Action | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **Export** | Pick what to include → set passphrase → share the file |
| **Import** | Open a `.shua` with the passphrase → appears as its own layer |
| **Layers** | Show / hide / rename / delete imported share layers |

Details: [Battle Graphics Share](#/battle-graphics-share).

### Share Overlay Screenshot

Shares a picture of the **map as it looks now** (current overlays and graphics included in the image).

### Share My Grid / Coordinate

From **Tools → More**: shares the inspected coordinate text (the grids you configured under Coordinate Format).

---

## Set values — formats and HUD

### Coordinate Format

Chooses which grids appear when you inspect a point (WGS84 / UTM / MGRS / related formats). Affects inspect panels and “share my grid”.

### Map Screen HUD

Controls on-map readouts:

- Crosshair coordinate formats
- Own-position formats
- Radial-menu **copy** values to clipboard

Tune this so the map shows only the numbers your team uses.

---

## This device

| Feature | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **Location Tracking** | Background location ON/OFF for tracks and sharing |
| **Kiosk Mode** | Lock the device so it stays in TacNav |
| **Hide Or Show Map UI** | Hide chrome/buttons for a clearer map |
| **Save Changes** | Persist drawings and layers on this device |
| **More** | Opens the overflow ops list (below) |

Device-owner / kiosk ADB steps live under **Device Ops** in this portal.

---

## More (overflow)

Opened from **Tools → More** — *Ops actions not on the main Tools list.*

| Feature | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **COMM** | Local platoon-net **demo** with ACP 125 brevity codes. Does **not** transmit on a radio by itself |
| **Share My Grid / Coordinate** | Share inspected coordinate text |
| **Personnel / COP / Tasks** | Ops / situational awareness menus (COP profiles, personnel, mission tasks, TAK status where configured) |
| **Device Health** | Map data version, location sharing, GNSS summary |
| **Capability Status** | Shows which TacMap capabilities are available vs gated on this build |

---

## Map chrome you will use every day

These controls sit on the map surface (not only inside Tools):

- **Location follow / center** — keep the map on you
- **Compass / north-up** — orient the map
- **Night mode** — dim UI for low light
- **Crosshair inspect** — tap or hold to read grids; copy from radial menu
- **Lib** chip — shortcut into Map Library
- **Layers** shortcut — same Overlays list as Tools

---

## Spatial Mesh on TacMap

When the **Spatial Mesh** plugin is installed, TacMap can show mesh radio markers, trails, and shared graphics. Mesh setup, channels, and private DM behaviour are documented separately:

→ [Spatial Mesh & LoRa](#/spatial-mesh-lora)

Without the plugin, TacMap still works; mesh shortcuts stay hidden.

---

## Limitations and coming soon

| Item | Status |
| --- | --- |
| **Troop Tracking** | Coming soon in Tools |
| **HERE WeGo** external turn-by-turn | Hidden / commented in code |
| **Path clearance / LOS** | Terrain visualisation only — not fire control |
| **COMM** | Local demo — not a radio replacement |
| **Download Map Area** | UI present; large offline packs need care |
| **ArcGIS road fallback** | Possible routing credits if OSRM fails online |
